title: Human-Computer Interaction: UI Evaluation Criteria and Methods
description: Covers interface evaluation criteria including usability and user experience, various evaluation methods such as interviews, cognitive walkthroughs, and Nielsen's heuristic evaluation, as well as safety and ethical guidelines.
content:
Chapter 5: Human Computer Interaction

1. Evaluation Criteria

USABILITY

Usability is about how easy, efficient, and effective a system is to use.

  • Quantitative: Measured through performance tasks (e.g., how many clicks, how much time it takes to complete an action).
  • Qualitative: Based on user opinions, feedback, and surveys (e.g., how simple or tiring the system feels).
  • Usability Survey: Often includes questions involving the ease of use, ease of learning, fatigue, simple preference, and other questions specific to the given interface.

USER EXPERIENCE (UX)

UX is more than usability it’s about the overall feeling, satisfaction, and emotional connection users have while interacting with the system. Covers how enjoyable, intuitive, and stress-free the app feels.

2. Evaluation Methods

  • INTERVIEW / OBSERVATION: The simplest way: talk to users or watch them use the system. Helps identify problems that designers might miss.
  • COGNITIVE WALKTHROUGH: Users “think aloud” while using the system. They describe what they are doing and why. This reveals their thought process and points of confusion.
  • EXPERT HEURISTIC EVALUATION: Usability experts review the system using established principles called heuristics.

Nielsen’s ten General UI heuristics:

  1. Visibility of system status
  2. Match between system and the real world
  3. User control and freedom
  4. Consistency and standards
  5. Error prevention
  6. Recognition rather than recall
  7. Flexibility and efficiency of use
  8. Aesthetic and minimalist design
  9. Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
  10. Help and documentation

MEASUREMENT

Collect numerical or survey-based data to measure effectiveness. Can involve time, error rates, or satisfaction scores.

3. Safety & Ethics

Evaluations must be safe and respectful. Users should give informed consent before participating. Participants should always have the right to stop whenever they feel uncomfortable.

Summary

Evaluating a user interface ensures that:

  • The system is easy to use (usability)
  • The experience is positive and enjoyable (UX)
  • The process is safe, ethical, and user-centered
